title: curated severity/progression literature pass, round 7 (PMC-OA dominant-sequela join) — three honest S/P lifts; one disclosed order-lock (5->6, +Phenylketonuria)

litcurate7_join.exact_sentence: Acute intermittent porphyria (AIP) is a rare metabolic disorder characterized by neurovisceral manifestations, most commonly severe abdominal pain.
Achondroplasia is a rare skeletal dysplasia characterized by severe disproportionate short stature.

PAH deficiency leads to hyperphenylalaninemia, with untreated blood Phe levels often exceeding 1200 μmol/L in classical PKU [ 2 ], resulting in severe intellectual disability and irreversible brain damage if not managed promptly [ 1 ].

litcurate7_excluded.considered_statement: The severest form of CAH results from an almost complete absence in enzyme activity that can lead to life-threatening salt-wasting (SW-CAH) in the first weeks of life and progressive virilisation if not optimally managed over time.
litcurate7_excluded.exclusion_reason: the retrievable OA disease-level severity framing for 21-hydroxylase-deficient CAH (C2936858) is FORM-SPECIFIC -- 'The severest form of CAH results from an almost complete absence in enzyme activity that can lead to life-threatening salt-wasting (SW-CAH) in the first weeks of life ...' attaches the 'life-threatening' magnitude to the SEVEREST FORM (classic salt-wasting SW-CAH), one allelic sub-form of the entity, not to the 21-OHD CAH entity as a whole, which also comprises the simple-virilizing classic form and the characteristically MILD non-classic (late-onset) form; the entity's own registry severity basis already records a 'variable severity spectrum (mild-to-severe range stated)', so no clean, isolable disease-level magnitude for the whole entity is retrievable (the life-threatening adrenal/salt-wasting crisis is the dominant untreated sequela of the CLASSIC forms only); S left [H], not lifted -- consistent with the umbrella/form declines recorded for alpha-thalassaemia, beta-thalassaemia and Hb SS

litcurate7_excluded.considered_statement: Male HFE C282Y homozygotes genetically predisposed to higher TSAT had a greater risk of haemochromatosis and severe clinical outcomes, such as liver and musculoskeletal complications, compared with those with genetically predicted low TSAT.
litcurate7_excluded.exclusion_reason: the retrievable OA severity framing for type 1 (HFE) hereditary haemochromatosis (C3469186) is COMPARATIVE and modifier-stratified -- 'Male HFE C282Y homozygotes genetically predisposed to higher TSAT had a greater risk of haemochromatosis and severe clinical outcomes ... compared with those with genetically predicted low TSAT' frames 'severe clinical outcomes' only as a BETWEEN-STRATUM contrast (high- vs low-TSAT-predisposed homozygotes), not as a clean disease-level magnitude for the HFE-HH entity's dominant untreated sequela (progressive parenchymal iron overload -> cirrhosis / hepatocellular carcinoma / cardiomyopathy / diabetes); the only other OA 'severe' framings retrievable are an HFE-C282Y HETEROZYGOTE case report (genotype-phenotype discordance, not the homozygous type 1 entity) and a non-dominant arthropathy hedge ('likely have an increased risk of severe chronic joint disease of the ankle'); type 1 HH is characteristically LOW-PENETRANCE (the entity's GeneReviews natural-history lexicon read 'mild', conflicting with the MedGen definition's 'severe' -- the source of the existing S 0.75 [H] grade), and no non-comparative disease-level magnitude is retrievable; S left [H] at value 0.75, grade NOT lifted
